content.title: About
content.content: Pecans are the edible seeds of the pecan tree (Carya illinoinensis), native to North America. Unroasted pecans have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. They are used in cooking, baking, desserts, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pecans belong to the hickory family and are closely related to the chestnut.
Indigenous peoples domesticated pecans more than 2,000 years ago.
The United States is the world’s largest pecan producer, especially the state of Georgia.
Pecans are a key ingredient in the classic Southern dessert pecan pie.
Unroasted nuts retain more natural antioxidants than roasted ones.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Pecans provide a high amount of heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains zinc and magnesium
items.content: These minerals support immune function, metabolism, and bone health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Abundant antioxidants
items.content: Pecans are rich in polyphenols that may help reduce inflammation.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Pecans can trigger allergic reactions in some individuals, potentially severe.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Because pecans are calorie‑dense, portion control is important.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Whole pecans can pose a choking risk for young children and should be chopped.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: People prone to kidney stones may need to limit pecan intake due to oxalates.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Unroasted pecans can be eaten as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or made into nut butter. They are also used in sauces and desserts. Soaking them for a few hours softens the texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store pecans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid.
